fundamental.thesis: Zydus Wellness is a mid-cap consumer wellness company (brands include Glucon-D, Complan, Sugar Free, Nycil and Everyuth). It has recently grown through debt-funded acquisitions: Naturell in India and Comfort Click in the UK for GBP 239 million. The latest extracted figures are stale and look inconsistent. The table labelled FY26 shows revenue of ₹396 cr (+46.2% YoY) and PAT of ₹20 cr (-43.2% YoY), but FY25 shows ₹2,709 cr. That suggests a mix of standalone and consolidated figures, or a quarter labelled as a full year. Even so, the direction is clear: EBITDA margin fell from 18.4% to 12.0% and PAT margin from 14.8% to 5.0%, while finance costs rose 718%. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-11-03 are not yet in the data. Using P/E as the yardstick, as the FMCG sector card does, valuation is expensive. Trailing P/E is 81.7x against a sector norm of 40–65x, EV/EBITDA is 38.5x (80th percentile, where 100 = most expensive), and ROE is only 3.4%. The forward P/E of 28.9x assumes a sharp earnings recovery, yet analysts cut their current-year EPS estimate by 21% in the last 30 days. Price is at 74% of the 52-week range, so the upside looks limited.

fundamental.thesis: Dalmia Bharat is a mid-sized Indian cement maker with 54.7 MTPA installed capacity across 12 states, expanding toward 67 MTPA, including the acquired Jaypee assets in Central India. Q2FY27 revenue, derived as H1 minus Q1 because the Q2 row is blank, was about ₹3,563 cr (+4.3% YoY, slowing from +10.7% in Q2FY26), and PAT was about ₹-201 cr after ₹339 cr of exceptional items; volume rose only 3%, EBITDA per tonne fell from ₹1,013 to ₹746, below the ₹900-1,100 healthy range, and management expects more fuel and Central India cost pressure in Q3. On the capital-intensive yardsticks of EV/EBITDA and EBITDA per tonne, I grade valuation fair: 12.3x EV/EBITDA is on depressed earnings, the 35.0x trailing P/E (Materials benchmark 12-22x) is distorted by one-offs, and the P19 EV/EBITDA and P15 P/B ranks are less useful because they compare against the broad market, not cement peers; the 15.7% position in the 52-week range offers some support, but this is not clearly cheap with FY EPS estimates cut about 19% in 30 days. The biggest risk is that fuel inflation and Central India dilution keep margins falling while capex of ₹3,200-3,400 cr continues, leading to further estimate cuts.

GMDCLTD is a Gujarat state-owned miner whose main business is lignite. Mining brings in nearly all its revenue (FY26 mining revenue ₹2,508 cr out of ₹2,653 cr total), and the loss-making power segment adds the rest. In Q2FY27, revenue from the official filing rose 71.2% YoY to ₹903 cr, faster than +23.8% in Q1FY27. Reported PAT fell 63.3% to ₹171 cr, but that is because Q2FY26 included a one-time ₹474 cr GST credit; without it, PAT grew about 27%. The PAT margin is 18.9%, close to Q1's 18.0% and well below FY26's 36% (which was inflated by the one-off). The quarter was strongly cash-backed: operating cash flow was 3.9x PAT and free cash flow ₹376 cr. Because this is a capital-heavy commodity miner, the right measure is EV/EBITDA, and the reported 43.9x is far above the 5–8x mid-cycle norm for cyclicals. However, that figure, the 163% dividend yield and the 4.47 debt/equity do not fit with Q1 EBITDA of ₹267 cr and the low liabilities in the segment data, so I treat them as unreliable. On the more dependable cross-check, trailing P/E of 20.6x is at the top of the 12–22x Materials range and P/B of 2.78x with 14.2% ROE is not cheap. Forward P/E (22.0x) is above trailing, which means earnings are expected to fall, so the grade is fair, not cheap, even though the stock ranks low on P/E against the broad market. The biggest risk is that the 71% revenue jump does not match the yfinance figure (₹538 cr), and it brought only modest underlying profit growth while margins shrank.

fundamental.thesis: NMDC Steel runs a single 3 MTPA integrated steel plant at Nagarnar, demerged from NMDC Ltd, and is still ramping up. The Government holds 50.79% and is looking for a strategic buyer. Revenue growth has slowed sharply from +129–179% during the ramp-up to +8.8% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹3,662 cr), but margins have turned around: EBITDA margin went from -37.9% (Q3FY25) to 7.9% (9MFY26) to 12.1% (₹442 cr), and PAT turned positive at ₹51 cr, up 97.6% YoY. Even so, the PAT margin is a thin 1.4%, the debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) is only 0.17, and finance costs of ₹126 cr took about 29% of EBITDA. We use EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for steel, because P/E means little on near-zero profit (235.6x). At 11.7x the stock looks expensive against the card's 5–8x mid-cycle range for steel, even though it ranks cheap (P17) against the broad market. That broad-market comparison is a fallback, not a true steel peer set. P/B of 1.05x is not a bargain when ROE is only 0.4%. The main risk is that profit stays too thin to cover heavy SBI loan repayments (₹3,177 cr outstanding, 30 quarterly instalments to 2031), with Q2FY27 results due on 12 Nov 2026 as a near-term binary event. The reported debt/equity of 35.02 is most likely a percentage (about 0.35x), which fits the loan size, so it is not a sign of extreme leverage.

fundamental.thesis: Abbott India is the Indian listed arm of Abbott. It is a branded-formulations franchise focused on the domestic market (Thyronorm, Duphaston and other women's health, gastro and chronic-therapy brands), so it is in the sector card's 'safe template' group with no US-tariff exposure. The only reliable figures are full-year FY26: revenue of ₹6,929 cr (+8.1% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,552 cr (+9.7% YoY), with a 27.7% EBITDA margin and a stable 22.4% PAT margin. Cash conversion was good but not excellent (CFO/PAT 0.85x, FCF ₹1,278 cr). The Q1FY27 yfinance row does not add up (₹932 cr revenue against a ~₹1,730 cr quarterly run-rate, and a 46% PAT margin), so I ignored it. The Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-11-05 have not been extracted yet, which means I cannot read the current trend. fundamental.thesis: CEAT is India's #4 tyre maker (global rank #4 by brand) with 51% replacement, 30% OEM, and 19% export mix, operating at 95% capacity utilisation across ~80,000 daily tyres — a capital-intensive ancillary with defensive replacement demand. Valuation looks outright cheap: EV/EBITDA at 7.4× sits at P5 vs the broad market (median 23.3×), trailing P/E of 20.2× is at P23 vs peers and -43% below market median — using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock screens as cheap, but the multiple compression is warranted given the margin collapse, and forward P/E of 15.1× implies the market expects earnings recovery, which is far from assured. The single biggest risk is that commodity costs (natural rubber, crude derivatives) persist or worsen into H2FY27, keeping EBITDA margins pinned at 9–10% and preventing the earnings recovery the forward P/E demands — a second consecutive quarter of PAT decline would trigger a meaningful derating.

fundamental.thesis: UPL is India's largest global agrochemical company, operating crop protection (UPL Corp), seeds (Advanta), and post-harvest segments across 130+ countries — a capital-intensive, leveraged cyclical recovering from a multi-year agrochem destocking cycle. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card guidance), UPL at 7.86× sits at P6 vs. 473 broad-market peers (67% discount to the 23.3× median) and at the mid-cycle floor for specialty chemicals (5–8× range); forward P/E of 12.65× is 46% below trailing 27.34×, signalling substantial earnings recovery priced in — the stock grades cheap on the appropriate metric. The primary risk is the combination of very high financial leverage (D/E flagged as extreme), NWC deteriorating sharply to 110 days (+24 days YoY from inventory build and FX translation), and persistent China-led price competition in agrochemicals — all amplified by rising crude input costs, INR weakness expanding USD-denominated debt service costs, and an ongoing RISK_OFF macro regime with FII net selling.

fundamental.thesis: Cohance Lifesciences is an Indian CDMO/API platform (formerly Suven Pharmaceuticals) serving global pharma innovators across Pharma CDMO, API+, Sapala nucleic-acid specialty chemicals, and Formulations — a niche franchise currently navigating a sharp operational trough driven by post-merger NJ Bio consolidation, Pharma CDMO order phasing, and Specialty Chemicals destocking. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue declined 23.1% YoY to ₹422 cr (decelerating sharply from +12.5% in Q1FY26 and extending the -13.1% full-year FY26 decline), with Pharma CDMO down 38.7% YoY, NJ Bio contributing an EBITDA loss of ₹328 mn, and PAT swinging to ₹-45 cr (-176% YoY); EBITDA margins imploded 2,220bps to 2.2%, though gross margins held at 71.5% and FCF remained a healthy ₹106 cr — indicating the trough is volume/timing-driven rather than structural margin destruction, and management has guided Q1FY27 as the floor with H2FY27 YoY recovery. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick per sector card guidance for a capital-intensive CDMO, the stock trades at 39.3× (P81 vs broad-market peers, 68% premium to median 23.3×), expensive on any normalised basis; trailing P/E of 88.6× (P91, distorted by the trough PAT) and forward P/E of 38.9× still sit well above sector Pharma medians of 28–40×, while sell-side FY EPS estimates have been cut 25.5% in the last 30 days — suggesting the recovery the market is paying for is actively being revised downward. The biggest risk is binary: an active FDA Warning Letter at the Nacharam FDF facility, if not resolved swiftly, could trigger customer qualification audits across the CDMO business precisely when the recovery pipeline depends on securing and delivering new orders against a backdrop of dangerously high Debt/Equity of 9.93.

Rainbow Children's Medicare runs a chain of 26 hospitals focused on children's and women's care (65% paediatrics, 30% women's care). Revenue growth has picked up for three quarters in a row, from +6.5% to +11.9% to +12.4% and now +23.2% YoY in Q2FY27 (₹548 cr), but profit grew only +10.9% to ₹84 cr. That is because PAT margin slipped from 17.0% to 15.3% and EBITDA margin from 33.5% to 31.0%, as 5 new hospitals with only 27.4% occupancy and a -16% EBITDA margin weigh on group profit. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a hospital business with heavy capital needs: at 26.1x it is only about 12% above the broad-market median (P59), and the forward P/E of 36.5x against a trailing 51.3x shows earnings growth is expected, so the stock looks fair, not cheap. The peer comparison is a broad-market fallback with no hospital peers in the set, and live data looks partly unreliable (24% dividend yield, D/E printed as 53.56), so the grade is only moderately confident. The main risk to the thesis is that profit lags revenue for longer than expected while new beds ramp up: analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 4% over 90 days even though all 14 still rate it a buy, a common pattern before a stock re-rates lower.

fundamental.thesis: Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands is a mid-cap branded apparel company that owns Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, plus a smaller emerging-brands portfolio. The main risk is profitability: net profit is only about 2% of revenue, and debt plus lease liabilities are high, so a weak festive season or slower same-store sales could wipe out much of the profit gain.

fundamental.thesis: HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is crude above $100 with a weakening rupee: marketing losses could return while the balance sheet is already stretched, with short-term borrowings up to ₹35,933 cr, a current ratio of 0.57, negative interest coverage and an ₹18,049 cr unrecognised LPG under-recovery.

IGL is the main city gas distributor in Delhi NCR, selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas (PNG) to homes and businesses. It is still adding volume: total volumes grew 6.9% YoY to 9.86 MMSCMD in H1 FY27, CNG rose 7.5% and domestic PNG rose 11.5%. Profits, however, have collapsed. H1 FY27 revenue grew 21.4% to ₹10,654 cr, but gas purchase costs jumped 39%, EBITDA margin fell from 12% to 3%, and PAT dropped 71% to ₹211 cr (a 2.0% margin). Q2 alone was much worse: EBITDA was negative ₹31 cr and PAT was about ₹26 cr, down roughly 93% from ₹386 cr a year earlier. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/E, as suits a capital-intensive utility. On those, the stock looks cheap: trailing P/E is 15.4x (inside the 10–18x utilities range), EV/EBITDA is 10.5x and the stock sits around the 12th–15th percentile of the market. But both figures are based on trailing earnings that are falling fast, and analysts have cut current-year EPS estimates by 50–59% in 90 days. So I grade it fair, and the low multiples may be a value trap. The biggest risk is that IGL cannot raise CNG and PNG prices to cover higher gas costs (in a politically sensitive Delhi market, with crude near $91 and rising), so margins stay crushed.

fundamental.thesis: J.K. Cement is a mid-sized cement maker that is also building a paints business through its subsidiary JK Maxx Paints. A new ₹130 cr, 75,000 KLPA plant in Telangana is funded from a ₹600 cr paints budget. In Q1FY27, revenue grew 20.3% YoY to ₹4,032 cr, but PAT fell 15.3% YoY to ₹275 cr. EBITDA margin has slid from 19.5% (H1FY26) to 17.0% and PAT margin from 7.5% to 6.8%, so volume growth is not reaching profits. The Q2FY27 results were filed on 2026-10-24 but have not been extracted yet, and the yfinance quarterly rows (₹513 cr revenue) are clearly inconsistent with the filings and were ignored. On valuation, I used EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business: 18.8× is below the broad-market median of 23.3×, but trailing P/E of 40.8× is far above the 12–22× Materials benchmark. Forward P/E of 25.6× depends on an earnings recovery that analysts are actively cutting (FY EPS estimates down 9.3% over 90 days), so I grade it expensive, even though cement usually commands a premium and the stock sits at 13.7% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is further margin compression in a crude-up, weak-rupee, risk-off environment, made worse by spending on paints, a segment the sector card describes as structurally broken by Birla Opus's entry.

Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% share of recent transmission bids, 29,802 circuit km of lines, a Mumbai distribution business, a fast-growing smart-meter business and a newly consolidated energy-trading platform. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr, a 13.1% PAT margin, after Q1 FY27 grew revenue 42.4% and PAT 124%. Two caveats apply to that growth: the H1 figures restate prior periods to include the energy-trading platform, and they count ₹4,961 cr of construction revenue (SCA, up from ₹3,692 cr). The extracted H1 rows also conflict (₹14,351 cr vs ₹19,787 cr). We grade valuation on EV/EBITDA plus P/B against ROE, the yardstick for capital-intensive utilities: EV/EBITDA of 25.1x, P/B of 7.2x on a 9.7% ROE and trailing P/E of 81.7x are far above the 10–18x utilities range, and the stock sits at 89.5% of its 52-week range. Analysts raising FY EPS estimates by about 16% in 30 days and a ₹87,222 cr transmission order book give good visibility, but the price already assumes flawless delivery. The main risks are leverage and execution: debt/equity is 1.84x, net debt is ₹41,067 cr, free cash flow is negative (₹-3,185 cr in H1), capex guidance is ₹21,000–25,000 cr a year, and Adani group news can move the stock regardless of results.

fundamental.thesis: Reliance Power is a midcap private generator with about 5.3 GW operating, mostly coal (Sasan ultra-mega plant with a long-term contract, running at about 92% load factor, plus Rosa). Only 145 MW is renewable, and another 4.8 GW of renewable and hydro capacity is stuck in the pipeline. In Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 3.8% YoY to ₹1,956 cr and PAT rose 44.9% YoY to ₹65 cr, a thin 3.3% PAT margin. This follows a FY26 loss of ₹337 cr, which came after a ₹38,160 cr asset write-down. The 'accelerating' revenue signal is mostly noise across quarters: growth has gone +12.2%, ~+1.5%, +0.5%, +3.8%, so the real picture is low-single-digit growth with no management guidance. I used EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a capital-heavy power company, plus P/B. At 8.3x EV/EBITDA (P8 vs the broad market) and 0.69x book, the stock looks cheap. But ROE is negative at -2.1% and interest costs eat about 18% of revenue, so a large part of the discount is a fair price for balance-sheet and governance risk, not a clear mispricing. The biggest risk is group solvency: auditors have flagged going-concern doubts, subsidiary RSTEPL has defaulted on about ₹2,296 cr of debt, and lenders have called a parent guarantee of about ₹1,842 cr for SMPL, which is now in insolvency proceedings. Any of these could wipe out the equity value that the low P/B seems to offer.

books.title: Fundamental grades → rules
books.hypothesis: Strong growers that are not yet decelerating, held whole and long: the one filter with measured forward information (+2.5 pp at 60 sessions, +5.6 pp at 120 vs the equal-weight universe in the point-in-time study), alone — kept at target weight and re-qualified every 120 sessions.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5

books.title: Book 6 bottom-up, neutral tilts (no model)
books.hypothesis: Book 6's construction with every sector tilt at 1.0, run live beside Book 6: the line the model tilt must beat by more than the random band (the bounds study of 26 Oct 2026 found no pack field beat it; the TWR line cannot judge the tilt, Book 6 − b6_neutral and the sector-call scorecard can).

rules.signal: monthly signal date recorded (rebalance cadence); NO sector_strategist call
rules.tilt: 1.0 for every sector, always (neutral = equal share over the sectors with eligible names or a holding)
rules.eligible: the shared fundamental filter: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes); ranked by revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.slots: 30 slots apportioned over the active sectors by largest remainder on w_s x 30 (sum = 30 exactly), with hysteresis: a sector's count changes only when its exact share moves > 0.5 slot from its current allocation; weight w_s / k_s each, capped at 2/30
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); rebalanced on the monthly signal date and on the flip
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions or exited in the last 20 sessions
rules.exit: fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high), or a tilt cut dropping k_s below the names held (lowest-ranked sold first); never on missing data, decelerating growth or timing
rules.rebalance: signal dates and the session the overlay flips; survivors outside +/-25% of target
rules.attribution: monthly Brinson vs the equal-weight universe (leaderboard key b6_neutral_attribution); no sector calls, so no scorecard
rules.judge: the comparator for Book 6: Book 6 − b6_neutral is the tilt's contribution

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
